card.intuition: Hallucination is confidently wrong model output with two flavors: factuality errors come from missing parametric knowledge (invented facts, wrong signatures, fake citations), while faithfulness errors come from output drifting away from context that is actually loaded. Next-token prediction produces fluent output whether or not the underlying fact is real, so an invented method arrives in the same assured register as a correct one and fails only when run.
card.analogy: A developer so fluent in the codebase that they 'remember' an API the codebase never shipped. They produce what the API would look like if it existed — plausible in a skim-level review, broken in production. Plausibility is not verification, so the only reliable check is running the code or reading the primary source.
card.time_complexity: O(C) per generated token over the full context window — hallucinated output is produced by the same next-token prediction as correct output, so deeper or doc-loaded contexts raise the per-request cost without raising correctness.
card.space_complexity: Context/memory footprint: the fix for factuality loads docs into the window, spending tokens and competing for the finite attention budget, which is exactly the mechanism that can trigger the faithfulness flavor.
when_to_use: Diagnosing wrong code: name the flavor — factuality (missing knowledge) or faithfulness (knowledge present but ignored)
Suspect fabrication: 'It hallucinated a parseAsync method on the schema' — check whether that method exists in context
Choosing a fix: add docs for factuality; clear or compact for faithfulness — the wrong fix makes it worse
Code review: treat plausible-by-construction code with suspicion until it is run or checked against a primary source
gotchas: Misdiagnosing faithfulness as factuality: pasting more docs grows the context and makes the drift worse
Do not use 'hallucination' as a bare synonym for 'wrong' — without naming the flavor the term has no diagnostic value
Check whether the correct information was already in context before deciding which problem you have

steps.label: Next-token prediction
steps.annotation: The generator produces fluent output whether or not the underlying fact is real.

steps.label: Invented method
steps.annotation: The model emits what the API would look like if it existed — plausible by construction.

steps.label: Confident register
steps.annotation: The model has no internal signal that it does not know something, so the guess sounds assured.

steps.label: Name the flavor
steps.annotation: If the correct info was never loaded it is factuality; if loaded but ignored it is faithfulness.

steps.label: Fix by flavor
steps.annotation: Factuality: load the docs. Faithfulness: clear or compact — adding more docs makes it worse.

steps.label: Check primary source
steps.annotation: Run the code or read the type definitions; a plausible signature only fails when executed.

exercise.prompt: Flag a fabricated API method: it is invented when it is absent from the real API surface.
hints: A method that exists in the real API is not a hallucination.
Compare the method name against the known set and return True when it is missing.
exercise.test_code:
assert is_fabricated('stringify') is False
assert is_fabricated('parseAsync') is True
assert is_fabricated('validate') is False
print('PASS')
